# The Conversation

> > Independent, evidence-based journalism written by academic experts and researchers, published under Creative Commons license across global editions including Australia, UK, US, Africa, Canada, New Zealand, and Indonesia.

The Conversation is a unique media outlet founded on the Academic Journalism Society model, where university researchers and subject matter experts write accessible articles on politics, environment, health, science, and culture. All content is freely republishable under Creative Commons licensing, serving both public education and media organizations worldwide.

## Key Topics

- Academic journalism and expert commentary
- Creative Commons licensing and republishing
- Climate change and sustainability
- Environmental conservation and wildlife
- Australian politics and governance
- Zoonotic diseases and public health
- Global editions (Australia, UK, US, Africa, Canada, NZ, Indonesia)
- Editorial independence and ethics
- Data protection and privacy compliance
- Energy policy and renewable resources
- Indigenous land management
- University research dissemination
- Evidence-based analysis
- Regional politics and security
- User-generated content standards

## About The Conversation

- [Editorial charter | The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/au/charter): Editorial charter defining journalism ethics and academic independence
- [¿Quiénes somos?](https://theconversation.com/catalan/who-we-are): About page for Catalan edition describing academic journalism mission

## Topic Areas and Regional Coverage

- [Environment + Energy – Views & Research – The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/au/environment): Australian environment section on climate, energy, and wildlife
- [Environment – Views & Research – The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/uk/environment): UK environment section covering climate, sustainability, and conservation
- [Politics – Views & Research – The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/africa/politics): Africa politics section covering governance, security, and regional affairs

## Featured Analysis and Commentary

- [The biggest estate on earth: how Aborigines made Australia](https://theconversation.com/the-biggest-estate-on-earth-how-aborigines-made-australia-3787): Aboriginal land management and fire-stick farming in pre-colonial Australia
- [2011: Year of the bat-borne virus](https://theconversation.com/2011-year-of-the-bat-borne-virus-4807): Analysis of Nipah and Hendra virus outbreaks in Bangladesh and Queensland
- [Chiropractic: crackers now, and crackers way back when](https://theconversation.com/chiropractic-crackers-now-and-crackers-way-back-when-4836): Critique of chiropractic as pseudo-science in Australian universities
- [ALP National Conference: Party reform the empty seat at the table](https://theconversation.com/alp-national-conference-party-reform-the-empty-seat-at-the-table-4562): Analysis of Labor Party factional politics and reform under Gillard
- [Gillard's reshuffle will not fool the voters](https://theconversation.com/gillards-reshuffle-will-not-fool-the-voters-4695): Political analysis of Gillard cabinet reshuffle and Labor voter support
- [House-brand push boils down to capitalism's crisis](https://theconversation.com/house-brand-push-boils-down-to-capitalisms-crisis-4467): Heinz CEO criticizes supermarket private-label brands and retail competition
- [Are banks gouging by not passing on interest rate cut?](https://theconversation.com/are-banks-gouging-by-not-passing-on-interest-rate-cut-4639): Analysis of ANZ/NAB response to RBA rate cut and banking profit margins
